blocks.text: The first episode is narrated within ancient understandings of hostile spirits and exorcism. It describes the man’s suffering and restoration in those terms; it should not be used to diagnose modern illness as demonic or to replace medical or mental-health care.

The Gerasene episode brings together a disputed location, the military-sounding name “Legion,” a large herd of pigs, liberation, fear, and the animals’ death. Readers have offered both historical and symbolic explanations for these details, but no single explanation is settled.

Mark places the woman’s healing inside Jairus’s urgent journey to his daughter, a recurring storytelling pattern in which one story is inserted into another so that the two episodes may interpret each other. Both women and girls are not merely background figures here: the woman acts as a petitioner and recipient of healing, while the child is restored. The preserved and translated words “Talitha cumi” also fit Mark’s practice of retaining several Semitic expressions.
